Coverage of small notation: checked every argument, index, exponent, equality, membership sign, tensor sign, O underline, prime, parenthesis, quoted phrase, accent, capital, punctuation and word ending. This includes all seven H^3 occurrences, the distinct H^1/H^0 pair, all 21 group-symbol positions, and all four tensor signs. These are visual coverage checks only, not proof checks.

The paper is one typescript sheet with pen mathematical additions, interlinear typed revisions, x cancellations, single underlines and blank reference brackets. The upper author/page number is 3 and the lower-left pencil archive number is 3. No date or written total page count occurs here. No independent diagram, figure, address, signature or marginal prose was found. Isolated scan speckles/edge marks were not promoted into textual content.

Hand identification is conservative: the packet does not independently identify the pen hand, so inventory labels it unnamed. The words doit, développer and géométrique are typewritten, even where their insertion connectors are pen. Deligne in the first reference is handwritten. Ordinary insertion hooks are represented by inserted markup at their attachment, not as independent figures.

Witness comparison: pure H macro conversions (emph to underline, add to inserted, struck to deleted, page number syntax) are not counted. H editorial notes were considered for their content: the tentative établir note prevents treating that word as wholly absent; the géométrique note explicitly marks placement/replacement uncertainty. Retained C doubts are included even when unchanged. Reordering or removing a doubt is flagged as a C difference. The added hand wrapper on the final subscript does not change the retained C alternatives.

Several H differences were already settled by the halves: quote shapes at uncropped phrases, the typed final r of retrouver, the comma after H^0(X,F), and the cancelled catég. Their changes entries explicitly say so; no unnecessary crop was made for a settled place. The main reader can make its own adjudication crops for these loci.

The page states a classification by a group pi_0, a commutative group pi_1 with action, and an arbitrary degree-three cohomology class; it mentions a Baer-style geometric interpretation of the H^3 group law. These are page statements, not results re-proved in this reading.

The examples state an expected recovery of the first Postnikoff invariant (on doit retrouver), give pi_0=H^1(X,F) and pi_1=H^0(X,F) with zero H^3 class in the strict Picard situation, and describe the automorphism/centre example. The possible novelty of k(C) is expressed tentatively as semble nouveau. The direct geometric link with Mac-Lane’s noncommutative extension/kernel theory is left to develop; no such link is established on this sheet.

Section 2 defines a Picard category by ACU structure and its underlying (Gr)-category, and strictness by identity self-symmetry on X tensor X. It says Deligne treats the corresponding champs de Picards, then discusses the additional commutativity and the compatibility issue for equivalences. The final action subscript was reread because its looped ink differs from H’s pi_1; the mathematical expectation was not used to erase the 0-like reading.
No mathematical proof, independent re-proof, computation, formal certificate, or consistency theorem was performed. math_checks is intentionally empty.
